newsitem.title: ITALY: France's Millon urges swift U.N. action on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France's Millon urges swift U.N. action on Zaire.

text.p: French Defence Minister Charles Millon called on Saturday for international intervention in Zaire "in the shortest possible time" after the U.N. Security Council put off a decision to send a humanitarian task force.
"I am among those who hope that (a decision) will be very rapid," Millon told a news conference in Florence after talks with fellow defence ministers from Spain, Italy and Portugal.
He said the catastrophe unfolding in eastern Zaire, where more than one million refugees from Rwanda and Burundi are at risk from fighting, "cannot wait".
France has pushed for an international force to go to the turbulent Central African region. Millon said its tasks should not only be humanitarian but also to help establish peace.
He said he could not comment on the reasons why countries on the Security Council, of which France is a permanent member, had sought to delay in a decision.
Establishing a multinational force "must come from a U.N. Security Council resolution" and France hoped it would be "voted in the shortest possible time", Millon said.
Early on Saturday the Security Council called on U.N. members to lay the groundwork for a multinational force but postponed its deployment until a later stage.
The interim resolution, adopted unanimously, asked the states involved to report back as soon as possible to enable the council to give final approval.
Many council members had hoped to adopt a resolution authorising the immediate creation of a multinational force to deal with a crisis that has already claimed thousands of lives.
This was impossible after the United States, mindful of its involvement in an ill-fated humanitarian operation in Somalia, said it was still studying whether and how it could participate.
Diplomats have said between 4,000 and 5,000 troops would be needed to carry out the mission.

France and Spain have already said they could send 1,000 men each. However, Rwanda's Tutsi government is mistrustful of France as an ally of the Hutu government ousted after genocidal massacres in 1994.
Millon refused to answer when asked about Rwandan objections to France in an interview before the news conference.

Millon and his southern European counterparts were in Florence to constitute a new four-nation rapid reaction force, Eurofor, which would be used for humanitarian and peacekeeping missions once it is fully operational.
Spanish Defence Minister Eduardo Serra Rexach called the situation in Zaire "chaotic and tragic" and said the Madrid government believed it required "action and a precious response".
Italy has not yet decided whether to commit troops to any force but Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta said military planners had already drawn up a contingency plan.
He said any mission had to be well-defined and have a clear mandate but added: "The time we have to avert a humanitarian disaster is very short".
